requestedActions.title: List active task titles, including pagination

guide.summary: Todoist documents OAuth2 authorization code flow for external apps to obtain user-authorized tokens. For read-only task listing, data:read is the documented least-privilege scope covering tasks. The app must be registered in the App Management Console with redirect URLs and client credentials before the first test. The GET /api/v1/tasks endpoint returns task content with cursor-based pagination, and the snippet does not confirm active-only filtering. Customer-admin approval and marketplace review are not addressed by the supplied sources.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List active task titles, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: OAuth2 authorization code flow issues user-authorized tokens to external apps
findings.detail: External applications obtain a user-authorized API token via OAuth2. The app redirects users to the authorization endpoint with client_id, scope, state and response_type=code, then exchanges the code at the token endpoint with client_id, client_secret and code.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their individual Todoist account.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data including tasks, projects, labels and filters. It does not grant create, update, complete or delete operations, matching the read-only confirmed request.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing active task titles for the connected individual account.

findings.detail: Developers must create the application in the App Management Console and configure one or more valid OAuth2 redirect URLs. The registered app receives a Client ID and Client Secret needed for the OAuth2 flow. Redirect URI is required when multiple URIs are configured.

findings.detail: For applications with refresh tokens enabled, which is the default for newly created apps, token responses include expires_in and refresh_token. Refresh uses grant_type=refresh_token at the token endpoint, and rotated refresh tokens are returned.
findings.appliesWhen: Token lifetime exceeds a single session for connected customers.

steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with the access token to read the first page. Read the task title from the content property of each results item and capture next_cursor. Only task titles are read; no write operations are performed. The supplied sources do not confirm active-only filtering, so do not assume it.
